passages.text: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.
passages.sermon: Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth about spiritual gifts.\r\nPaul says, “If I speak in the languages of people, or even of angels, but I do not have love, I am nothing more than a noisy gong.\r\nI am only a clanging cymbal.”
passages.original: Ἐὰν ταῖς γλώσσαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαλῶ καὶ τῶν ἀγγέλων ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω γέγονα χαλκὸς ἠχῶν ἢ κύμβαλον ἀλαλάζον

passages.text: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians about spiritual gifts.
He describes the importance of love.
If I have the gift of prophecy, I can speak messages from God.
If I understand all mysteries, I know every secret thing.
If I have all knowledge, I know everything.
If I have complete faith, I can move mountains.
If I do not have love, I am nothing.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἔχω προφητείαν καὶ εἰδῶ τὰ μυστήρια πάντα καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γνῶσιν καὶ ἐὰν ἔχω πᾶσαν τὴν πίστιν ὥστε ὄρη μεθιστάναι ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω οὐθέν εἰμι

passages.text: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul describes actions without love.
If I give everything I own to the poor, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
If I give up my body so I can boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ψωμίσω πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντά μου καὶ ἐὰν παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου ἵνα καυχήσωμαι ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω οὐδὲν ὠφελοῦμαι

passages.text: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
passages.sermon:
Love is patient.
Love is kind.
Love does not envy.
Love does not boast.
Love is not proud.
passages.original: Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ χρηστεύεται ἡ ἀγάπη οὐ ζηλοῖ ἡ ἀγάπη οὐ περπερεύεται οὐ φυσιοῦται

passages.text: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.
passages.sermon:
Love is not rude.
Love does not seek its own way.
Love is not easily angered.
Love keeps no record of wrongs.
passages.original: οὐκ ἀσχημονεῖ οὐ ζητεῖ τὰ ἑαυτῆς οὐ παροξύνεται οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν

passages.text: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.
passages.sermon: Love does not rejoice in evil.\r\nLove rejoices in the truth.
passages.original: οὐ χαίρει ἐπὶ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ συνχαίρει δὲ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ

passages.text: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
passages.sermon:
Love bears all things.
Love believes all things.
Love hopes all things.
Love endures all things.
passages.original: πάντα στέγει πάντα πιστεύει πάντα ἐλπίζει πάντα ὑπομένει

passages.text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.
passages.sermon:
Love never fails.
Prophecies will end.
Tongues will stop.
Knowledge will pass away.
passages.original: Ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε πίπτει εἴτε δὲ προφητεῖαι καταργηθήσονται εἴτε γλῶσσαι παύσονται εἴτε γνῶσις καταργηθήσεται

passages.text: For we know in part and we prophesy in part, but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.
passages.sermon:
We know only part of the truth now.
We prophesy only in part now.
We do not have complete knowledge.
We do not have complete prophecy.
The perfect will come in the future.
When the perfect comes, the partial will end.
The incomplete things will pass away.
passages.original: ἐκ μέρους γὰρ γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται

passages.text: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking about spiritual maturity.
When I was a child, I spoke like a child.
I thought like a child.
I reasoned like a child.
When I became an adult, I put away childish things.
I no longer acted as a child.
passages.original: Ὅτε ἤμην νήπιος ἐλάλουν ὡς νήπιος ἐφρόνουν ὡς νήπιος ἐλογιζόμην ὡς νήπιος ὅτε γέγονα ἀνήρ κατήργηκα τὰ τοῦ νηπίου

passages.text: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
\r\nHe explains our current understanding of God.
\r\nRight now, we see only a dim reflection.
\r\nIt is like looking into a mirror that does not show everything clearly.
\r\nWe do not see the full truth yet.
\r\nOne day, we will see face to face.
\r\nNow, I know only in part.
\r\nThen, I will know fully.
\r\nI will know just as God fully knows me.
passages.original: βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι δι’ ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον ἄρτι γινώσκω ἐκ μέρους τότε δὲ ἐπιγνώσομαι καθὼς καὶ ἐπεγνώσθην

passages.text: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians about what is most important for Christians.
Three things remain for us.
These three things are faith, hope, and love.
Love is the greatest of these three.
passages.original: Νυνὶ δὲ μένει πίστις ἐλπίς ἀγάπη τὰ τρία ταῦτα μείζων δὲ τούτων ἡ ἀγάπη
